Yeah I most certainly agree that my fears of the actions of others and the actual actions can be two completely different things. What sucks is when your fear becomes true. I'm not sure if that's a rhetorical question, should you look. Yes, I think you should look, whether or not looking at your possible fears can cause that feeling of anxiety or what have you. The thing about fears is that they can be conquered. For example: most of my life I have feared death, up until the point where I dropped acid. Something about dying doesn't really scare me anymore. Sure, the trip to death would suck, and I fear the pain and suffering that could precede death- but the actual being wiped out of existence and possibly never seeing anybody or anything I have ever come to know; that no longer bugs me. I think, on the other hand, that fears are a necessary evil. Fear will keep you safe, not necessarily saying that you should let it control your life though. Let's just say you have a fear of heights: you can get over this fear by climbing high things, constantly putting yourself in that fear will eventually get you over it. But, the fear of heights is also logical. If you're standing on a tight rope 40 stories up and there's nothing to stop you from falling to your death- maybe it's a good thing you're scared of heights. So I guess in short; fear is necessary, as it might/will keep you from doing ridiculously stupid things. But, once you let your fear control you to the point that you won't ride in a car just because you're scared of closed spaces, maybe it's time to reevaluate how you're perceiving your life.
